result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers explain the gamut limit and avoid simply siding with the printer. B sets expectations more clearly by aiming for 'clearly the same orange' rather than an exact match, and it adds useful extras: a ready-to-send message to the printer, a brand-notes record of the print values, and a caveat that the numbers are starting points. A gives a sharper diagnosis of the brown tint (cyan or black in the mix) and names a well-chosen Pantone, but it uses more jargon (ICC, FOGRA39, GRACoL) and says less about what result to expect. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers explain the screen-versus-ink limit and treat the printer's reply as only partly true. A is better at setting expectations: it says outright to aim for a close match rather than an identical one, and it warns against judging color from a PDF or screenshot. A also uses less jargon. B gives strong diagnostic questions and a well-chosen Pantone 1585 C, but it brings in ICC profiles and FOGRA39/GRACoL and only briefly says an exact match isn't possible.
